items.title: MACC rubbishes report senior Umno leader to be called up after assembly
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has rubbished reports that a senior Umno leader is expected to be called up for questioning after the party's general assembly. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said there was no such individual on the commission's radar. "As far as I'm concerned, and as far as MACC is concerned, there is none.

items.title: Former company GM on remand for alleged power abuse
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A former general manager of a real estate investment holding company is on remand for two days until tomorrow on suspicion of abusing his position to secure benefits and rewards. Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin issued the remand order against the man, who is in his 30s, following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Shah Alam magistrate's court here. According to a source, the suspect was arrested at about 2pm yesterday at the Selangor MACC office.

items.title: '33-vote support for senator candidate shows Perak unity government remains strong'
items.summary: IPOH: The unanimous 33-vote support among state government representatives for Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri as a senator reflects the strong and stable cooperation among its component parties. Perak PKR information chief and spokesman Azam Afandi said the support was more than just a mandate for Hairul. He said it showed that cooperation among the parties which form the state unity government remained harmonious.

items.title: As election looms, Sweden's government is paying immigrants to leave
items.summary: ONCE known for its welcome to migrants, Sweden has not only shut its borders over the last decade, its right-wing government is now paying some foreign-born residents to leave, part of a tough stance on migration it hopes will help it secure reelection this month. As countries across Europe clamp down on immigration, Sweden has made one of the most drastic about-turns. Since the start of 2026, the Swedish coalition government, which took power in 2022 on a pledge to cut immigration and crime, has been offering those with residency permits from outside the European Union up to 350,000 Swedish crowns (US$37,000) if they leave the country.

items.title: AI Governance Bill expected to be tabled in Parliament by Q1 2027 at the latest
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill being drafted by the Digital Ministry is expected to be tabled in Parliament this quarter or by the first quarter of next year at the latest, said Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo. He said the draft bill had been completed after the ministry conducted workshops and engagement sessions to obtain views from stakeholders, and was now in the process of being submitted to the cabinet. Previously, the ministry, through the National AI Office (NAIO), began engagement sessions throughout July to refine the proposed AI Governance Bill, as part of the government's efforts to introduce and enhance understanding of the governance framework that will form the basis for the proposed bill.

items.title: Pilot's wife sends heartfelt message after husband's death in heli crash
items.summary: That was the message from Izzati Syamimi, wife of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, to her husband's friend, Alexson Adit Henry, 31, who was also killed in the helicopter crash at the STOLport in Long Lellang, Sarawak, two days ago. Izzati left the message in the comments section of a Threads post by Alexson's wife, Stephanie Essah. Stephanie had shared a family photo of herself, Alexson and their two children, Candy and Ivan.

items.title: M360 Asean bridge differences, advance shared digital future - Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: M360 Asean can serve as a regional platform for governments and industry players with differing stances to convene, deliberate and identify common ground to advance Asean's digital future, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi said that this is the very role envisioned for the event as governments, regulators and industry players navigate the opportunities and challenges arising from the region's digital transformation. Touching on Asean's digital prospects, Fahmi said the effective implementation of the Asean Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) could propel the regional digital economy to USD2 trillion by 2030.

items.title: Connectivity, public trust must advance together for inclusive digital Asean
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Echoing Malaysia's drive for an equitable and secure regional digital ecosystem, Asean nations must accelerate connectivity while bolstering public trust to ensure rural and remote communities are not left behind. Indonesian Communication and Digital Affairs Ministry secretary-general Dr Ir Ismail said government intervention remained necessary in areas where building telecommunications infrastructure was not commercially viable for private operators. Ismail said Indonesia's geographical complexity, encompassing more than 17,000 islands, required the government to support common infrastructure, including terrestrial networks and satellite connectivity.

items.title: PAS at Umno assembly: Friendly visit or ‘preview’ of next election?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — When PAS delegates began arriving at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur last night for Umno’s annual assembly this week, the gesture drew more than polite greetings from party members. For some Umno delegates, the presence of PAS delegates was a sign that the idea of Malay-Muslim unity was gaining ground again. For others, it was a matter of returning a courtesy after Umno representatives attended PAS’s muktamar last week.

items.title: All UiTM endurance challenge patients allowed home, except one
items.summary: MARAN: The sole endurance challenge participant initially treated in the Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) Intensive Care Unit (ICU) has been transferred to a general ward. The student is among nine Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) students hospitalised after experiencing breathing difficulties during the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge at the UiTM Jengka campus on Sept 4. Of the three students admitted to Hoshas, one died on Sept 5, while another was discharged on Sept 7.

items.title: Country Heights unit faces RM55mil asset auction
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Country Heights Holdings Bhd unit Country Heights Commercial Development Sdn Bhd (CHCD) faces a judicial auction of a 2.60-hectare commercial property in Kajang, Selangor, with a reserve price of RM55 million. The latest reserve price represents a reduction of RM14.85 million, or 21.26 per cent, from the previous RM69.85 million reserve price. Country Heights said the property had a carrying value of about RM33.5 million based on CHCD's latest available financial statements.

items.title: Nepal flood death toll tops 1,410 as search for survivors continues
items.summary: "The rescue and search work in the tunnels at Trishuli 3A, 3B and Chilime hydropower projects is ongoing," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP. In Nepal, 1,367 bodies have been recovered and 5,132 people are missing, its disaster authority said on Wednesday. In China, 43 people are dead and 519 are missing, according to state media.

items.title: Blackstone buys majority stake in South Korean logistics park
items.summary: BENGALURU: Blackstone said on Thursday it has acquired a majority interest in Sanha Logistics Park II, a dry storage logistics development in South Korea, through a primary share issuance, as it seeks to deepen its presence in the East Asian nation. Sanha Logistics Park II, a storage development spanning 334,000 square meters, is currently under construction and is expected to be completed in 2028. The total development cost of Sanha Logistics Park II is approximately 600 billion Korean won (US$448.30 million), ESR told Reuters.

items.title: Four Indonesian volcanoes record 13 eruptions as activity continues
items.summary: JAKARTA: Four Indonesian volcanoes, including Anak Krakatau, recorded at least 13 eruptions on Thursday as volcanic activity continued across the archipelago, with ash from one volcano keeping an airport in East Nusa Tenggara closed. The Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation Centre (PVMBG) said as of midday, six eruptions were recorded at Mount Ibu in North Maluku, four at Ili Lewotolok in East Nusa Tenggara, two at Semeru in East Java and one at Anak Krakatau, which erupted at 9.10am Western Indonesian Time. However, the eruption column at Anak Krakatau was not observed.

items.title: Four Chinese nationals face kidnapping charge after Singaporean allegedly held for RM3.28m ransom
items.summary: BALIK PULAU, Sept 10 — Four Chinese nationals were charged at the Sessions Court here today with kidnapping a Singaporean man in July and demanding a ransom of SGD1 million (about RM3.28 million). The accused, Liu Ting Jun, 46; Huang Jian, 39; Wang Hao Yu, 32; and Guan Siqi, 24, the only woman among them, however, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to them in Mandarin before Judge Ahzal Fariz Ahmad Khairuddin. According to the charge sheet, the accused, as well as two others still at large and another two individuals who have since died, are accused of jointly abducting and wrongfully confining Quek Aik Teng at the Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas at 4.15 pm on July 26.

items.title: Techna-X admits listing breach over undisclosed RM45m Hong Kong asset sale
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Techna-X Bhd has admitted to breaching Bursa Malaysia's listing rules after failing to announce a previously executed RM45.0 million agreement to dispose of its 50 per cent stake in Hong Kong Aerospace Beidou New Energy Technology Co Ltd (HKAB). Nong, who already holds a 15 per cent stake in HKAB, subsequently defaulted on payment terms, leading Techna-X to terminate the deal on July 10, 2026. Techna-X first invested in HKAB in October 2020, injecting RM41.66 million.

items.title: Drug syndicates use public as mules to smuggle cannabis to Europe, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: BACHOK, Sept 10 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have found that drug trafficking syndicates operating by air to Europe frequently use members of the public as drug mules, particularly to transport cannabis flowers, which are in high demand on the continent. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department Director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said, however, that not all pilots arrested for involvement in drug smuggling were transporting drugs to Europe. He said most air-based drug trafficking cases involving Europe centred on cannabis flowers due to the high demand for the illicit substance in the market.

items.title: North Korea leader's daughter believed to have younger sibling
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's daughter and apparent successor is believed to have a younger sibling, South Korea's spy agency said on Thursday, offering a more detailed view of the ruling family's structure. Kim's daughter, Kim Ju Ae, was first introduced to the public in 2022 when she accompanied her father to the launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile. Since 2022, Kim Ju Ae has appeared at a number of major political events with the North Korean leader, including a high-profile visit to Beijing.

items.title: Layang-Layang Aerospace voluntarily grounds BO-105 fleet after Sarawak helicopter crash
items.summary: Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the decision was taken by the operator voluntarily and should not be interpreted as an indication of technical failure. Norazman said CAAM records showed that the helicopter’s Certificate of Airworthiness was valid until Aug 4, 2027, while its Certificate of Registration remained valid until July 28, 2029. Norazman said CAAM was monitoring the operator’s grounding and inspection programme, while also verifying the relevant regulatory, operator and pilot records.

items.title: Cops need months of intelligence to bust drug lab syndicates
items.summary: BACHOK: Operations to dismantle drug syndicates, particularly those involving clandestine drug laboratories, require months of intelligence gathering to ensure the entire network is uncovered before raids are carried out. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police took time to track how precursor chemicals brought into the country were being used to manufacture drugs. Hussein said gathering intelligence was complex and required continuous monitoring of suspected individuals and locations.

items.title: Pakistan says no military response discussed under Mecca pact over Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan said on Thursday that there were no discussions about a military reaction from Islamabad under the Mecca agreement in response to the Houthis' attacks on Saudi Arabia, but added that Pakistan will "act" when the "time comes." The comments by Pakistan's foreign ministry spokesperson came in response to a question on how Islamabad plans to fulfill its obligations under a joint defence accord it signed with Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. When time comes (we) will act under the agreement," foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said at a weekly media briefing.

items.title: Online scam committee findings heading to cabinet soon - Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Findings from a series of discussions by a special working committee tackling online scams will be presented to the cabinet soon, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said a cabinet note was being prepared to outline several key decisions reached following the committee's engagements. Fahmi described the committee as unique as it brings together commercial banks, telecommunications companies and digital platform providers, including TikTok, for the first time in a coordinated effort to combat online scams.

items.title: Court rejects police bid to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand, former TH chairman set for release
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim is expected to be released this evening after his remand period was not extended, said his lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad. He said the police’s application to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand period for another three days to assist in the investigation under Section 420 of the Penal Code had been rejected, and the former Baling Member of Parliament is expected to be released before 5pm this evening once the previous remand period expires. Abdul Azeez and two former TH officers were previously remanded for two days to assist in the investigation into a fraud case related to TH hibah.

items.title: [UPDATED] Sarawak Flying Doctor Service suspended after helicopter crash
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: All Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in Sarawak have been temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash involving an aircraft used for the service in Long Lellang. Dzulkefly said the MoH would conduct a comprehensive assessment of the overall FDS service delivery framework in Sarawak, including contracts, governance, operational safety, coverage requirements and the effectiveness of the existing service delivery model. Yesterday, Dzulkefly said the government would continue operating FDS to ensure healthcare coverage for remote communities.

items.title: Azam: Tei's lock-up attire, handcuffs complied with MACC procedures
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki maintained that requiring businessman Albert Tei to wear lock-up attire and handcuffs complied with prescribed procedures and was not unconstitutional. In an affidavit replying to Tei's originating summons, Azam, who retired in May, said the requirement was governed by MACC Chief Commissioner's Directive No. He said the directive required detainees to wear MACC lock-up clothing at MACC offices and when taken out for investigations or court proceedings, including remand hearings where detainees must be handcuffed.

items.title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected across KL, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm today. It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Kuala Muda, Baling, Sik, Yan and Langkawi in Kedah; Timur Laut, Barat Daya, Seberang Perai Utara and Seberang Perai Tengah in Penang; and Kuala Pilah, Seremban, Jempol and Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan. Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Larut Matang, Selama, Bagan Datuk, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Sepang, Petaling, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Klang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, as well as Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut and Lipis in Pahang.

items.title: Petronas moves to unlock stranded oil, accelerate exploration & production
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) is stepping up efforts to unlock Malaysia's marginal and stranded hydrocarbon resources, with two new upstream initiatives aimed at accelerating exploration and production. Through Malaysia Petroleum Management (MPM), Petronas has awarded the Estuary Cluster small field asset production sharing contract (SFA PSC) to Harvester Energy (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, while handing over seismic data for the Mutiara Cluster to support further exploration. MPM senior vice-president Datuk Ir Dr Bacho Pilong said the Estuary Cluster PSC award reflected Petronas' continued focus on unlocking discovered resources through innovative and fit-for-purpose development solutions.

items.title: Asean eyes single submission model for medical device approval
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed Asean Single Submission Model for the pre-market approval of medical devices could move towards implementation once member states agree to the initiative. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal is currently being put forward as an agenda item, with Asean countries contributing input and sharing best practices on its implementation. On bilateral engagements, Dzulkefly said Malaysia had reinforced its Memorandum of Understanding on Health Cooperation with Singapore, expanding collaboration in digital health, active ageing and regulatory reliance between the Medical Device Authority and Singapore's Health Sciences Authority.

items.title: Sarawak Flying Doctor Service operations suspended after fatal helicopter crash, says health minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — All Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in Sarawak have been temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Miri, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said today. “Emergency medical evacuation services for urgent cases will continue through cooperation between the Health Ministry and the Fire and Rescue Department,” he said. Dzulkefly said the ministry would also discuss the possible use of Armed Forces assets to transport patients requiring emergency treatment to suitable healthcare facilities.

items.title: Anwar, Kelantan MB discuss stronger ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud to discuss ways to strengthen ties between the federal government and the opposition Pas-ruled state. In a social media post, Anwar said the meeting covered federal support in several areas, including infrastructure, the economy, agriculture, education, healthcare and social amenities. "(This is) including support in various sectors, such as infrastructure, the economy, agriculture, education, healthcare and social amenities to ensure the state's development continues smoothly," said Anwar.

items.title: King presents appointment letters to two judges
items.summary: The ceremony began with the presentation to Court of Appeal judge Alice Loke Yee Ching, followed by High Court judge Elaine Yap Chin Gaik. She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on July 10, 2020. She was elevated to Shah Alam High Court judge on Jan 17, 2023, before being appointed to the Kuala Lumpur High Court's Special Powers Division on Aug 18, 2025.

items.title: HE Group secures RM25mil power systems order
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HE Group Bhd's unit Hexatech Engineering Sdn Bhd has received a purchase order valued at RM25 million. The purchase order commences on the date of acceptance and is targeted for completion in 20 weeks. Barring any unforeseen circumstances, the purchase order is expected to contribute positively toward HE Group's future earnings and will not affect the group's share capital or substantial shareholders.

items.title: King grants audience to higher education minister, PSC chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today granted an audience to Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir at Istana Negara. According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page, during the audience session, His Majesty agreed to be presented with the current developments of the Sultan Ibrahim Malay Studies Chair at Beijing Foreign Studies University (BFSU). Meanwhile, Zambry in a Facebook post said the Sultan Ibrahim Malay Studies Chair at BFSU reflects His Majesty's concern and patronage towards efforts to expand studies and strengthen the position of the Malay language, culture and civilisation on the international stage.

items.title: 'I would give my life to bring them back,' man loses wife, two sons in Kluang fire
items.summary: Those were the heartbreaking words of Khairul Nizam Wahid, 50, who lost his wife and two sons after fire engulfed their double-storey terrace house in Taman Titiwangsa last night. His wife, Noraini Ibrahim, 49, and sons Khairul Nurhaziqq Khairul Nizam, 18, and Khairul Nurhadif, 11, were found dead after the blaze broke out at 10.30pm. Khairul Nizam said he had returned home after going out for a drink with a neighbour when he saw the sofa in the living room on fire.

items.title: Umno Youth wants government to reintroduce GST
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to immediately reinstate the Goods and Services Tax (GST), as the system is more transparent and efficient than the Sales and Services Tax (SST). Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said available data showed that revenue collected under the abolished tax system was significantly higher. Umno Youth thanks you.

items.title: 'Over 100 PPR tenants on eviction list, but Penang government not cruel'
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: More than 100 tenants of the Taman Manggis People's Housing Project (PPR) units are on the eviction list after losing eligibility for Penang's PPR housing. The Penang government, however, said it was not acting cruelly. State Housing and Environment Committee chairman Datuk S. Sundarajoo said the cases were carefully assessed and genuine hardship would be considered on a case-by-case basis.

items.title: Sarawak heli crash: Remains of Alexson to be brought Desa Senadin after post-mortem
items.summary: MIRI: The family of the late medical assistant, Alexson Adit Henry, 31, who died in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang on Tuesday is still awaiting the results of the autopsy before setting a date and time for his last respects and burial. On Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) announced that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport). Apart from Alexson, the other victims who died were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, and two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.

items.title: Digital Ministry seeks Budget 2027 incentives to cut cost of digital tools for small traders
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 10 — The Digital Ministry has proposed incentives under Budget 2027 to make digital tools more affordable and encourage their adoption among small traders, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said today. He said the proposals were presented during a meeting with Finance Ministry officials two weeks ago as part of the government’s Budget engagement process. “Let the Finance Ministry make its decision and the prime minister announce it during or before the Budget,” he said.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh confirms Pardons Board meeting as speculation over Najib’s bid mounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has confirmed that the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) will convene tomorrow morning. “Yes, I can confirm that tomorrow at 8.30am, there will be a pardons board meeting. FMT previously reported that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application is expected to be among the primary matters tabled before the board during this week's sitting.

items.title: Puteri Umno wishes Najib well ahead of expected clemency bid discussion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno’s women’s youth wing, Puteri Umno, today extended its best wishes for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid ahead of a meeting expected to discuss his application. This follows a report by Free Malaysia Today that the Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s clemency application during its meeting this week. Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi expressed the wing’s positive wishes during a press conference at the Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL) today.

items.title: Zahid to meet Negeri Sembilan MB over statement on proclamation involving Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today he will meet Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim during the party’s general assembly to seek an explanation over his statement regarding a proclamation involving the state’s ruler. Zahid said Ismail would meet him during the assembly, which began yesterday, although he did not specify when the meeting would take place. Asked when the meeting would take place, Zahid said: “The general assembly has already begun.

items.title: Umno president Zahid says being optimistic about Najib’s pardon chances tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said he was hoping for the best when the Pardons Board considers former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid tomorrow. The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s latest application for tomorrow. Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine.

items.title: King presents appointment instruments to Court of Appeal, High Court judges
items.summary: The ceremony began with the presentation to Court of Appeal judge Alice Loke Yee Ching, followed by High Court judge Elaine Yap Chin Gaik. She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on July 10, 2020. She was elevated to Shah Alam High Court judge on Jan 17, 2023, before being appointed to the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Special Powers Division on Aug 18, 2025.

items.title: Perak Assembly approves PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul as senator with 33 votes
items.summary: IPOH, September 10 — The Perak Legislative Assembly today approved the appointment of Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri as a senator after he secured 33 votes in a secret ballot. The 38-year-old defeated Perak PAS Dewan Ulama chairman Muhammad Zulkifli Muhammad Zakaria, the Opposition coalition’s candidate, who received 26 votes. Mohamad Hairul has also served as Perak PKR chairman since 2024.

items.title: Transboundary haze discussed on sidelines of Asean health ministers meeting, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The transboundary haze issue is not on the formal agenda of the 17th ASEAN Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings, but it is being discussed on the sidelines among health ministers of member states. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the matter could subsequently be taken up at the senior officers’ meeting. However, Dzulkefly said the issue could be addressed within the scope of the existing health clusters.

items.title: Dr Akmal: Umno Youth ready to work with PAS in Melaka, state is next test for Malay-Muslim unity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno Youth is ready to work with PAS in the coming Melaka state election and believes its support among young voters can help deliver another electoral victory, Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said today. So I ask Datuk Seri (Zahid), Melaka should be blue as well,” he said during his speech at the Umno Youth general assembly.He said Umno Youth was prepared to repeat the strong performance it recorded among young voters in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections. Dr Akmal said the wing was prepared to cooperate with PAS in Melaka, while making clear that he was not seeking candidacy for himself.

items.title: Malaysia’s unsold completed homes rise 8.6pc in H1 2026, but market is resilient, says Finance Minister II
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — More completed homes and serviced apartments were left unsold in the first half of 2026 compared with the preceding six months, according to the Property Market Report for the First Half of 2026. The report, released by the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) today, showed that the number of unsold completed homes rose by 8.6 per cent, from 30,471 units in the second half of 2025 to 33,094 units in the first half of 2026. Residential properties accounted for 59.3 per cent of all transactions, with 110,998 deals recorded, and contributed 44.8 per cent of the total transaction value, or RM47.11 billion.

items.title: Dismissing royal pardon powers undermines Federal Constitution, says Puteri Umno chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi today said that challenging or dismissing the royal power to grant pardons directly undermined the Federal Constitution. During her keynote address at the Puteri Umno General Assembly, held in conjunction with the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, Amal described the royal institution as a key pillar of national sovereignty. Also present were Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.

items.title: Kangar Bersatu deputy chief, 90 branch chiefs leave party over loss of trust in leadership
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 10 — Kangar Bersatu division deputy chief Faisol Rahman, together with the division committee and 90 of its 99 branch chiefs, announced tonight that they are leaving the party with immediate effect. Also announcing their departure were the division’s Armada, Srikandi and Srikandi Muda leadership lines, including Armada Kangar deputy chief Mohd Firdaus Ismail and all Armada committee members. “Having spent so long building the party at the grassroots level, we feel that trust in the party’s leadership has been lost,” he said.

items.title: MOH still awaiting official post-mortem report on five Long Lellang crash victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is still awaiting the official report on the post-mortem findings of the five victims who were killed in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was still awaiting official confirmation on the matter before providing further details to the public. Also present were MOH secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad and Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abdul Wahab.

items.title: Digital minister says Malaysia’s draft AI Governance Bill complete, hopes to table it by Q1 2027
items.summary: He said the government was now setting up the structure needed to enforce the proposed law. Gobind said the government must establish the agencies and administrative structure needed to monitor compliance and enforce the law before it takes effect. Gobind said the proposed legislation would form part of a broader AI governance framework combining technical standards, regulations and laws.

items.title: Nurse killed in helicopter crash had planned to leave flying doctor service to further studies
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 10 — The dream of nurse Jessie Paya Jok, 44, to further her studies was cut short when she was killed in the flying doctor service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday. Her close friend, Caroline Sawai Joseph Chungat, 43, a nurse at Miri Hospital, said Jessie, or more fondly known as Paya, had told her that this month would be her last assignment with the FDS. “That was the last conversation between Paya and me last month.

items.title: No hazardous API readings recorded nationwide, Sarawak records highest unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — No areas recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to haze as of 9 am today. Meanwhile, four areas in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Larkin (140), Kluang (125), Batu Pahat (115) and Pasir Gudang (114). In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda also recorded an unhealthy API reading of 167.

items.title: Alam Maritim CEO charged with fraud over vessel charter rates, claims trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Azmi Ahmad was charged in the Sessions Court here today on two charges of fraud relating to the daily charter rate of a vessel. According to the first charge, Azmi is charged with defrauding TH Alam Management Sdn Bhd principal officer Iskandar Mohd Zaffa, 48, by concealing the actual offer of Daily Charter Rate dated August 24, 2023 which allocated RM80,500 per day in the Work Order. The act allegedly prompted Iskandar to agree to sign the BIMCO Supplytime 2017 with a Daily Charter Rate of RM70,000 per day between Alam-JV DP2 (L) Inc. and Alam Maritim (M) Sdn Bhd.

items.title: ‘Flabbergasted’: Lawyer says lock-up attire, handcuffs were not former TH chairman Abdul Azeez’s choice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim’s lawyer has rejected the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) assertion that his client chose to appear in court wearing a purple lock-up shirt and handcuffs yesterday. In a statement, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad said police instructed Azeez to change from his normal clothes into purple lock-up attire and handcuffed him before taking him to court for a remand hearing. After a two-day remand order was granted, Amer said Azeez was taken directly to another courtroom for the MACC charge to be read without being given an opportunity to change.

items.title: ‘No need to erase history’: Wanita Umno defends Najib’s legacy amid ‘legal process’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The women’s wing of Umno has reaffirmed its loyalty to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, asserting that the party does not need to “erase history” to build its future. Speaking at the Wanita Umno general assembly today, the wing’s chief, Datuk Seri Noraini Ahmad, urged the party to appreciate leaders who devoted their lives to the service of Umno and the nation. “And Wanita Umno also does not forget the contributions of Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak.

items.title: Ceiling fire at Jengka Hospital wards forces 17 to evacuate, no injuries reported
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 10 — Part of the ceiling in the paediatric and women’s wards at Jengka Hospital caught fire last night, but all 17 individuals in the wards escaped unhurt. Wong said initial information from Pahang JBPM indicated that the fire originated above the ceiling of the two wards, causing about 10 per cent damage to the wiring and ceiling structure.

items.title: Man dies after suspected heart attack, falls into septic tank pit in Kota Bharu
items.summary: Kota Bharu Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) chief Mohd Ridwan Baharuddin said the department received an emergency call at 5.28 pm. Firefighters extricated the victim using a stretcher before Ministry of Health medical personnel examined him, he said last night. Initial assessments by the medical team suspect the victim suffered a heart attack before collapsing,” he said.

items.title: NRD: 365 foreigners charged over fake MyKad, birth certificate offences in eight months
items.summary: PORT KLANG, Sept 10 — The National Registration Department (NRD) disclosed that 365 foreigners were charged in court over MyKad and birth certificate fraud between January and August this year. Enforcement director Mazhad Abdul Aziz said 738 joint operations were conducted with various agencies nationwide, including raids on premises and factories to detect the use of fraudulent identification documents. “Of that number, 286 cases involved the use of fake identity cards or cards belonging to others, while another 79 were linked to forged birth certificates.
